Ninety Percent of the Light

STS-HS9-L2-10001300-HSSCIPHY-RWS-LAT-01 • HS Physical Science • Photovoltaic Materials and Light Absorption
Look at the picture. You will answer some questions about it. Press the play button to hear each question. Record your answer for each question. You can listen to your answer and record it again. Click SUBMIT RECORDINGS when you have answered all the questions.
JUST FOR FUN · OPTIONAL
When Hurricane María knocked out Puerto Rico's power grid in 2017, a community group in the mountain town of Adjuntas kept its lights on with solar panels it had installed years earlier. Neighbors walked in to charge phones, refrigerate insulin, and buy bread from the one bakery still running. Volunteer solar brigades then trained ordinary residents to mount and wire panels on their own roofs, so the next storm would not take the whole town dark.
A solar panel is almost black. What do you think would happen to the electricity it makes if someone painted it white?
